sectionHeadings: 026: Repair backup retention, restore ordering, validation and configuration failure
B-1. One predicate decides what a backup file is
B-2. The retention floor is stated in the zone it is compared in
B-3. A restore stages the replacement before destroying anything
B-4. A follower moves its state aside rather than deleting it
B-5. Validation checks the image and returns errors
B-6. The purge is bounded, the retry count is counted, and the S3 configuration names what is wrong
B-7. The supported restore topology is N=1, and this says why
B-8. An interrupted restore is rolled forward, never onto a database without its WAL
B-9. A backup is finished and durable before it has its name
B-10. Retention never deletes the newest backup
record.summary: Repairs F-056 through F-063. One predicate decides what a backup file is, a restore stages the replacement before destroying anything, a follower moves its state aside instead of deleting it on an environment variable alone, validation checks integrity and returns errors instead of panicking, the post-restore purge is bounded, the S3 configuration names the variable that is wrong and proves its credentials before a restore, and two reporting contradictions are corrected. States N=1 as the supported restore topology and says why N=3 is not.
record.title: Repair backup retention, restore ordering, validation and configuration failure
